newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dealers greet Buba repo exemption, split on impact.
newsitem.headline: Dealers greet Buba repo exemption, split on impact.

text.p: Money traders on Thursday welcomed the Bundesbank's decision to exempt certain securities repurchase, or repo business from minimum reserve requirements.
The move helped reduce a disadvantage that Germany had against rival financial markets like London and could thereby lead to some repo business returning to Frankfurt, they said.
But the dealers were divided on the extent to which the repatriation of repo business would happen.
Money market interests rates, meanwhile, were not expected to be affected by the move since the impact of the change on banks' liquidity would not be great enough, dealers said.

"It's a step in the right direction because the German market is at a disadvantage compared with London and Luxembourg," said Werner Bauer, head of money and foreign exchange trading at Bethmann Bank.
"But it will be hard to get back the business that we lost."

One money dealer who declined to be named said: "It was expected. We welcome it of course, it will help to strengthen Frankfurt as a financial centre and it will contribute to winning repo business back from abroad.
It will make life easier for us as bankers and make it easier to trade bonds in Frankfurt."
Many German banks had repo trading desks in London as well as Frankfurt and such double desking may now become unnecessary, the trader said.
Banks may decide to run just one repo desk, and since reporting lines went to Frankfurt, it may make sense for that desk to be in Frankfurt, the trader said.
"The move was expected, it came as no surprise but the easing of the burden for the money market is not so great that it will affect money market rates," one money trader said.
"I don't expect an impact on the money market. Call money rates are still unchanged at 3.00/3.05 percent."

In a widely expected move designed to enhance Germany's standing as a financial centre, the Bundesbank said on Thursday it would exempt maturities repurchase agreements with maturities of up to one year from minimum reserve requirements from January 1, 1997.
The central bank the move would only lead to a small cut in the overall minimum reserve requirement, the Bundesbank said.
